152:### 9. `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS` — extend the 1.5s ceiling on the user's 14 SessionEnd audits
153:
154:- **Value:** The user has **14 SessionEnd hooks** (settings.json:810-905, lines 815-895) running async telemetry: claude_md_count_audit, cite_drift, mcp_self_audit, mcp_overhead, skills_cite, phantom_reference, rotate_jsonl, agent_frontmatter_audit, tmp_md_inventory, tmp_promote_authoritative, process_hygiene_audit, memory_persist, ccusage_session_telemetry, codex session-lifecycle. Each has `timeout: 30` declared, but **CC 2.1.105 changed the ceiling to 1.5s regardless of declared timeout** — fix landed in CHANGELOG:1265 with the env var override. Without this env, the user's 30s timeouts are silently capped at 1.5s — explaining the long-running observed audits that "appear to start but don't finish" (the 12 hooks at line:818-895 are most affected).
155:- **Source URL:** `Z:/repos/deps/claude-code/CHANGELOG.md:1265` ("Fixed `SessionEnd` hooks being killed after 1.5 s on exit regardless of `hook.timeout` — now configurable via `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS`").

162:- **Risk:** **LOW** — extending the ceiling never *forces* hooks to take longer; it only allows declared timeouts to be honored. If a hook genuinely deadlocks, a 60s ceiling means session-exit waits up to 60s instead of 1.5s. Acceptable trade-off given the user's audit-trail discipline.

140:- **Verification:** README @ SHA `1452b1ca8aa194bb60a4bd19e77d06a8e82ead40` §Windows §"Native Windows (limited support)" + §Auto-Rewrite Hook.
141:
142:#### Critical Windows caveat (verbatim from upstream README §Windows)
143:
144:> "On native Windows (cmd.exe / PowerShell), RTK filters work but **the hook does not auto-rewrite commands**: `rtk init -g` falls back to **CLAUDE.md injection mode** — your AI assistant receives RTK instructions but commands are not rewritten automatically."
145:>
146:> | Feature | WSL | Native Windows |
147:> |---|---|---|
148:> | Auto-rewrite hook | Yes | **No (CLAUDE.md fallback)** |
149:> | `rtk init -g` | Hook mode | CLAUDE.md mode |
150:
151:**Implication:** the savings table in the README (60-90%) reflects WSL-with-hook performance. Native-Windows-CLAUDE.md mode means Claude *sees* RTK instructions but the bash hook does not rewrite Bash tool calls — agents must explicitly type `rtk git status` instead of `git status`. The user's environment is Git Bash on Windows (not WSL).
152:
153:#### Install command transcript
154:
155:```bash
156:# 1. Pre-check (verify already-installed binary)
157:"Z:/claude/bin/rtk.exe" --version
158:# Expected: rtk 0.37.2
159:
160:# 2. Run upstream init from inside claude-sota (per README §Auto-Rewrite Hook §Setup)
161:cd /z/claude-sota
162:"Z:/claude/bin/rtk.exe" init -g --auto-patch
163:# This will: (a) inject RTK.md into CLAUDE.md, (b) attempt PreToolUse hook in settings.json
164:# On native Windows: only (a) succeeds — (b) falls back per README
165:
166:# 3. Inspect the diff BEFORE committing
167:git -C /z/claude-sota diff CLAUDE.md .claude/settings.json
168:git -C /z/claude-sota status
169:
170:# 4. Verify install
171:"Z:/claude/bin/rtk.exe" init --show
172:# Expected (native Windows): "RTK.md: found" + "settings.json: hook present (CLAUDE.md fallback)"
173:```
174:
175:#### Wiring details (what `rtk init -g` writes — per README + `rtk init --show` output today)
176:
177:| File | Native Windows behavior | T1 surface? |
178:|---|---|---|
179:| `Z:/claude-sota/CLAUDE.md` | RTK.md content injected (markers `<rtk-managed>...</rtk-managed>`) | YES |
180:| `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/settings.json` | PreToolUse hook entry attempted; falls back to CLAUDE.md mode | YES |
181:| `Z:/claude-sota/RTK.md` | New file | YES (new design-surface file) |
182:
183:#### Verification probe
184:
185:```bash
186:# Probe 1: binary smoke
187:"Z:/claude/bin/rtk.exe" gain --format json | head -5
188:
189:# Probe 2: confirm CLAUDE.md mention exists

191:

194:# expect: JSON OK
195:
196:# Probe 4: end-to-end — restart CC, ask agent to run 'git status' on a small project, then check rtk gain
197:# (Manual; native Windows agents will only invoke rtk if instructed via CLAUDE.md, hook does not auto-rewrite)
198:```

201:
202:- **Medium**. Native-Windows mode reduces savings ceiling vs WSL claims. CLAUDE.md injection adds ~50-200 lines of RTK guidance (token cost) — measure first-turn context delta with `ccusage` (A1) before/after.
203:- Reversible via `rtk init -g --uninstall` (per README §Uninstall).

3:## Token optimization is architecture, not shorter prompts
4:
5:Best stack:
6:
7:```text
8:measurement:
9:  ccusage
10:  statusline
11:  devtools
12:  cross-code-organizer
13:
14:shell-output compression:
15:  RTK
16:
17:semantic retrieval:
18:  Serena
19:  Claude Context
20:
21:repo capsule:
22:  Repomix
23:
24:large-output sandbox:
25:  Context Mode
26:
27:cross-agent compression/memory:
28:  Headroom
29:
30:read-path/context profiling:
31:  Wet
32:  Distill
33:  Skinny Jeans
34:  Whetstone
35:
36:docs/browser:
37:  Context7
38:  Playwright MCP
39:```
40:
41:## Default stack
42:
43:```text
44:ccusage
45:RTK
46:Serena
47:Repomix
48:rg / fd / jq / yq / gh
49:```
50:
51:## Important distinction
52:
53:RTK optimizes shell output. It does not optimize Claude Code built-in reads/searches.
54:
55:Therefore pair:
56:
57:```text
58:RTK       -> Bash output
59:Serena    -> symbol-level code navigation
60:Repomix   -> controlled repo snapshots
61:Skills    -> progressive disclosure
62:Subagents -> noisy exploration isolation
63:Worktrees -> file isolation
64:```
65:
66:## Context admission policy
67:
68:Before context enters the model, ask:
69:
70:```text
71:Is this needed now?
72:Can it be summarized deterministically?
73:Can a symbol/reference answer it?
74:Can a focused command answer it?
75:Can a subagent inspect it and return only findings?
76:Can it live in a Skill or supporting file?
77:```
78:
79:## Anti-patterns
80:
81:```text
82:giant CLAUDE.md
83:always-on MCP buffet
84:memory plugins before durable memory
85:whole repo dumps every turn
86:cat huge logs
87:multi-agent swarm reading same files
88:```

5:## Core rules
6:
7:- Use semantic code retrieval before reading many files.
8:- Prefer `rg`, `fd`, `jq`, `yq`, `git diff --stat`, `git diff --name-only`, focused tests, and small logs.
9:- Never dump full logs or whole repositories into context.
10:- Use worktrees for parallel sessions and large tasks.
11:- Use subagents for noisy exploration, research, verification, and review.
12:- Use Skills for repeat workflows instead of expanding this file.
13:- Run focused tests before broad tests.
14:- For risky changes, run Claude review plus Codex review/adversarial review.
15:- Treat plugins, MCP servers, hooks, memory tools, dashboards, and bridge tools as executable software requiring source audit.
16:- Prefer durable memory: GitHub issues, PRs, ADRs, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, skills, repo maps, and task files.

.claude\rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:113:   - **(a) Atomic temp-rename for FULL-FILE writes ONLY**: write to `<path>.tmp.<nanos>.<pid>`, then `os.replace` (cross-platform atomic on POSIX + Windows NTFS). Use ONLY for FULL-FILE write-once classes where last-writer-wins is acceptable (e.g., `codex_review_HEAD_<sha8>.txt` written once per commit, `codex_consult_<topic>_<pid>.txt` written once per consult). NEVER use this option for SHARED JSONL append targets — `os.replace` does atomic file-swap but does NOT merge concurrent appends, so two writers concurrently doing read-modify-replace can drop earlier records (lost-update race). For NO-CLOBBER first-write semantics, use `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)` for exclusive creation; fail closed (caller catches) if collision detected.
.claude\rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:114:   - **(b) Filename-namespace**: include `<agent_id8>` or `<process_id>` in filename so concurrent writers cannot collide on the same path (e.g., `codex_review_HEAD_<sha8>_<agent_id8>.txt` or `codex_consult_<topic>_<pid>.txt`). Consumers must merge across the namespace if a unified view is needed.
.claude\rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:115:   - **(c) Lockfile + O_CREAT|O_APPEND atomic-write for SHARED JSONL append**: open the JSONL log with `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | os.O_WRONLY, mode)` where `mode` defaults to `0o600` (owner-only — per Round-5b T3 round-3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS trust-boundary finding on commit `c2b5dee`: `0o644` was world-readable and leaked audit-trail content (agent prompts, PIDs, verdict cite paths, `agent_id` UUIDs, T1/T2/T3 verdict bodies) on multi-user hosts. Callers MAY opt-in to `0o640` group-readable for shared-CI cases via explicit `mode=` argument + documented umask interaction (e.g., `umask 0o027` for CI runner) — `0o644` is REJECTED as default for any audit-trail JSONL). **Migration semantic for legacy files** *(Round-7 amendment per T3 round-4 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.91 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `df37fb1`; closes non-migrating gap caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE — POSIX `os.open` applies `mode` ONLY when `O_CREAT` actually CREATES the file)*: pre-existing files at `0o644` (created under Round-3-through-5 mandates pre-Round-6) RETAIN their world-readable perms after open, leaving the audit-trail leak intact unless coerced. After every `os.open`, the caller MUST: (i) read `current_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.fstat(fd).st_mode)`; (ii) if `current_mode != mode` AND the file is owned by caller-uid, call `os.fchmod(fd, mode)` to coerce existing file to the mode invariant; (iii) if `os.fchmod` raises (`PermissionError` due to read-only mount, alien owner, ACL conflict on Windows NTFS, etc.), FAIL CLOSED — propagate the exception rather than proceeding with non-conforming perms (the audit-trail invariant is enforced everywhere or fails loudly). Document in commit body for any consumer applying this rule: one-time migration shell command `find .claude/state -name '*.jsonl' -perm /044 -exec chmod 0600 {} +` (POSIX) OR `Get-ChildItem -Path .claude/state -Filter *.jsonl -Recurse | Where-Object { ($_ | Get-Acl).AccessToString -match 'Everyone Allow Read' } | ForEach-Object { icacls $_.FullName /inheritance:r /grant ${env:USERNAME}:F }` (Windows) for legacy `mcp_health.jsonl` / `subagent_transcripts.jsonl` / `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` / `subagent_start.jsonl` / `worktree_lifecycle_audit.jsonl` files created at `0o644` per pre-Round-6 mandates. The `O_CREAT` flag ensures a missing log auto-creates rather than failing the first writer; **if `os.open` raises (read-only mount, permission denied, disk full), the exception MUST propagate — do not catch-and-ignore** (per Round-5 F-1 silent-failure finding). Take an **exclusive advisory lock** (`fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` on POSIX / `msvcrt.locking` on Windows); **if neither primitive is available, or if the platform does not enforce advisory locks (e.g., NFS without NLM support), FAIL CLOSED — raise rather than proceeding without a lock** (per Round-5 F-2 NFS-silent-succeed finding). **Windows separate-lockfile mechanism** *(Round-7c per T3 round-7b NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `48c49fb` caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE)*: `msvcrt.locking` locks `nbytes` from CURRENT file-pointer position, NOT the whole file like POSIX `fcntl.flock`. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Module returns `lock_fd` for Windows callers to release; `None` for POSIX. **Lock-protocol rollout constraint** *(Round-7c per same T3 finding)*: when the lock protocol bumps (direct-jsonl-fd → separate-lockfile-v1, or separate-lockfile-v1 → separate-lockfile-v2-versioned), enforce single-version deployment for the entire concurrent-writer cohort. Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Currently sss has ZERO consumers of `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` (FORWARD-REF wire-up Ships 2-5 pending per `tmp/wave22-orchestrator-salvage-jsonl-mode-bits-audit-2026-05-05.md`), so the version-skew window is THEORETICAL until first hook migrates to use the module. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). After the write, `os.fsync(fd)` if durability is part of the contract (audit-trail JSONL needs fsync; ephemeral telemetry may skip); **if `os.fsync` raises (`EIO`, `ENOSPC`), propagate the exception — do not silently ignore a durability failure when durability is contracted** (per Round-5 F-4 fsync-failure finding). Use for SHARED JSONL log targets (`mcp_health.jsonl`, `subagent_transcripts.jsonl`, `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` class) where consumers expect interleaved appends from multiple writers and unified-view semantics are required.

docs/v64-stable-prefix-convention.md:79:**Hash-domain canonicalization** (per Wave 84 codex T1 F-2 P2 fix-forward): `stable_prefix_hash` covers ONLY the in-message-stream prefix content (system + developer + initial_user messages + any in-stream project_context up to `prefix_frozen_at_message_index`).
